text:
marta: Heads-up — customer ACME missed PII-containing requests during an audit. Their route /v1/exec-high only sampled at 0.01 and we ended up with 1 sample for the whole window. Audit needed ~10.
aj: Oof. Was sampling sticky to tenant/route? I thought we had per-route sticky sampling + quota-awareness.
marta: It was sticky but the tenant quota was exhausted; system fell back to global low-sample. Ops couldn't raise it fast enough. We need a breakglass flow for short-term forensics without permanent config changes.
kevin: We already have an "inspect" canary but that's more for controlled rollouts and requires console perms. Idea: console issues a short-lived "inspect token" that temporarily overrides sampling for a scoped tenant/route. Token should be auditable.
sam: Also want a visual: show a sampled-density heatmap on the route page so PMs/SEs can see coverage over time (samples/hour, PII-risk-weighted).
telemetry-bot: current-config snippet: `sampling: { rate: 0.01, sticky: true, quota_group: "tenant-ACME" }`
aj: Proposal sketch: add a "Raise samples (breakglass)" button on route -> modal asks: rate, duration, reason, approvers. Action emits audit log and requires 2 approvers. Default scope = tenant.
marta: Default to scoped tenant. Also show PII risk score for the window; only allow breakglass if legal flag is present or approver list includes compliance.
oncall-sre: From oncall POV: need CLI/HTTP API to do this too for fast incident response. Something like `rictl sampleset --route /v1/exec-high --rate 0.2 --ttl 30m --reason "forensics" --audit-header "INC-1234"`. Must produce an audit event with requestor and approvers.
kevin: Implementation notes: RBAC + expiry + console visibility. Storage note: if we increase sampling, do we backfill missing data? Backfill is expensive. Maybe we only capture forward and expose an "on-demand backfill" job.
sam: Backfill = heavy. Alternative: a short full-capture mode (encrypted) for a TTL (e.g., 24h) that stores blobs accessible only via explicit audited console flow. Encryption keys access audited via KMS logs.
aj: Edge cases: capping cost during breakglass. Add a token cap (e.g., max 10k tokens or X requests) and stop capture after cap; emit alert.
marta: And critical: redaction must still run even in breakglass. We can't allow plaintext PII exports. Any captured payloads go through scrub pipeline and are flagged. Exports require separate legal workflow.
kevin: I'll draft a short RFC with API shape, CLI sample, console mock, and telemetry wireframes. Will include migration plan for sticky sampling map. Any objections to 2-approver model?
sam: :thumbsup:
oncall-sre: We'll add a runbook entry and an alert if breakglass used >3 times in 24h for same tenant/route. Also require enum'd reasons in audit.
marta: Can we surface a sampling-coverage metric in Console: e.g., %routes with median sample >= 0.05 and per-tenant sampled requests/hour? That helps prevent surprises.
aj: Also need a rolling migration for existing sticky sampling keys so breakglass respects previous opaque keys. I'll write rollout steps.
kevin: Action items: 1) I'll write RFC draft (API + console + CLI + RBAC) by EOD Friday. 2) @aj to draft heatmap wireframe. 3) @oncall-sre to add runbook skeleton. 4) @telemetry-bot to produce current coverage snapshot for last 7d.
marta: Thank you. Please include example policy snippet in RFC for reviewers:```
# example temporary override
override: {
  scope: "tenant:ACME",
  route: "/v1/exec-high",
  rate: 0.2,
  ttl: "30m",
  approvers: ["ops:alice","legal:bob"],
  audit_reason: "forensics-INC-1234"
}
```
aj: One more thought — telemetry should tag samples with `capture_mode=breakglass` so queries can filter and we can compute impact/cost.
marta: Great. Let's keep PII safety as default-first. No plaintext downloads without legal. Meeting if needed on Monday to finalize the UI copy for the modal.
kevin: I'll post RFC link when ready.
sam: thanks all
